source_first80_paragraphs.visible_text:
For HELP on using this form: comprehensive instructions can be found at 
http://www.3gpp.org/Change-Requests.
Latency bound requirement of NR SL CSI report

Use one of the following categories:
F  (correction)
A  (mirror corresponding to a change in an earlier 													release)
B  (addition of feature), 
C  (functional modification of feature)
D  (editorial modification)

Detailed explanations of the above categories can
be found in 3GPP TR 21.900.

Use one of the following releases:
Rel-8	(Release 8)
Rel-9	(Release 9)
Rel-10	(Release 10)
Rel-11	(Release 11)
…
Rel-16	(Release 16)
Rel-17	(Release 17)
Rel-18	(Release 18)
Rel-19	(Release 19)

If sl-LatencyBoundCSI-Report is configured with a value smaller than minimum UE’s processing time (TSLproc, 1) defined in TS 38.214, the SL-CSI report will always be cancelled based on MAC spec, section 5.22.1.7.
2> if the sl-CSI-ReportTimer for the triggered SL-CSI reporting expires:

For example: when µSL is 1, TSLproc, 1 is 5 slots. If sl-LatencyBoundCSI-Report is configured with 3, which is smaller than minimum physical layer processing time TSLproc, 1. From MAC layer point of view, the sl-CSI-ReportTimer will always expires and cancel the SL-CSI report.
Add reference to RAN1 spec (TS 38.214) in field description of sl-LatencyBoundCSI-Report. A UE is not configured with a value smaller than minimum UE’s processing time.
If the UE is implemented according to this CR and the network is not, the UE may be configured with unexpected NR SL CSI reporting parameters.
If the network is implemented according to this CR, and the UE is not, there is no inter-operability issue.
If the UE is implemented according to this CR and the other UE are not, the UE may be configured with unexpected NR SL CSI reporting parameters.
